newsitem.title: FRANCE: French culture minister said firm on media reform.
newsitem.headline: French culture minister said firm on media reform.

text.p: France's new communication and culture minister, Catherine Trautmann, is expected to outline on Wednesday plans for making important changes in the French media sector, an adviser at the culture ministry said.
The adviser told Reuters on Tuesday that recent comments by Trautmann showed she was determined to push through certain changes, but would not rush into taking hasty decisions.

"The Prime Minister will outline the strategic aims in various sectors on Wednesday and each minister will get down to work," the adviser said, giving no details of timing or order of priority for the reforms.

Trautmann said on Sunday France's new government wanted to reintroduce a 25-percent limit on the shareholding any one shareholder can possess in a media company. The previous centre-right government had increased the limit to 49 percent.

Shares in media firms and their parents have been hit on the Paris bourse since the beginning of the week, but dealers say news of the reform plans, flagged in newspaper Le Monde a week ago, is now largely reflected in share prices.
"The most important point is limiting concentration. In all European countries there are anti-trust laws which are more or less efficient," Trautmann told a weekly debate on RTL television and radio.

"For the moment we do not have a sufficiently clear and efficient system in France, notably in relation to investment by companies which win public contracts, and which can today intervene in a quasi-majority way. We want to bring back the 25 percent limit," she said.

She also said she wanted to review an accord under which public television channels France 2 and France 3 are broadcast exclusively on digital satellite service Television par Satellite (TPS), operated by TF1.
If such an exclusive deal were to be outlawed, France 2 and France 3 would also be broadcast on rival satellite service Canalsatellite, owned by Canal Plus. DT/SLA
